angle_en: Anushajjate: the wise do not cling to good works
angle_hi: अनुषज्जते: ज्ञानी अच्छे कर्म में भी आसक्त नहीं होता

en.intro: Listen for one verb. It shows how a wise person acts without attachment to results.
en.notice: Listen for one verb, anushajjate, clings to. The wise one does not cling to wholesome action, the very thing most people chase. This is how a renunciate acts.
en.next: Krishna now explains why total renunciation is impossible for any embodied being.
en.meaning: One who neither rejects unwholesome action nor clings to wholesome action is a wise renunciate, free of doubt and established in clear seeing.

hi.intro: एक क्रिया पर ध्यान दीजिए। यह बताती है कि ज्ञानी व्यक्ति बिना फल की आसक्ति के कैसे कर्म करता है।
hi.meaning: जो अकुशल कर्मसे द्वेष नहीं करता और कुशल कर्ममें आसक्त नहीं होता, वह त्यागी, बुद्धिमान्, सन्देहरहित और अपने स्वरूपमें स्थित है।
hi.notice: एक शब्द सुनिए, अनुषज्जते, यानी आसक्त होना। ज्ञानी व्यक्ति कुशल कर्म, यानी अच्छे काम, में भी आसक्त नहीं होता, जो कि लोग अक्सर चाहते हैं। यही सच्चे त्यागी का काम है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब बताते हैं कि शरीर में रहकर कर्म का पूर्ण त्याग किसी के लिए संभव नहीं है।

issues: meaning_changed: "Listen for one verb. It shows the difference between a true renunciate and someone who is merely running away from the world." (The English intro contrasts the true renunciate with 'someone who is merely running away from the world,' which contradicts the meaning of verse 10. The verse describes a wise person who acts without attachment to results, not someone running away. This misrepresents the verse's core message.)

meaning_changed: "The wise one does not cling to wholesome action, the very thing most people chase." (The English notice states that most people chase wholesome/good action. However, the source text (and the previous verse 9) indicates that people typically chase the fruits/results of action, not the wholesome action itself. This introduces an unsupported generalization that shifts the meaning.)

borrowed: "Krishna now explains why total renunciation is impossible for any embodied being." (This is the content of the NEXT verse (18.11), not this verse (18.10). The intro/notice is presenting the content of the following verse as if it were the current verse.)
